Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: first-person point-and-click castle exploration game background. Generate ONE full-bleed landscape 1536x1024 image, 3:2. The SAME inhabited medium-sized western fantasy lord's castle throughout: fine realistic painted environmental concept art, pale warm-gray limestone ashlar and restrained pointed arches, deeply textured dark oak, small aged bronze fittings, muted wine-red cloth and natural linen where suitable. Beautiful tactile materials, crisp legible architectural edges, coherent rigid perspective and believable human-sized construction. Standing eye-level viewpoint, natural wide angle, complete readable room with foreground depth, finished environmental painting. Soft cool daylight balanced with small warm household light, calm cared-for lived-in atmosphere, no exaggerated palace scale. No people, readable words, UI, navigation arrows, hotspot outlines, return-button graphics, watermark, collage, modern objects, magical effects, banners with heraldic emblems or named-world symbols. Keep the architecture functional and coherent.
Scene: the ENCLOSED TOWER STAIRWELL reached from the upper guest corridor, ascending toward the tower-top lookout. Camera has just passed through the guest corridor's pointed pale-stone opening and stands on a level stone landing; that lower entrance is BEHIND the camera and not visible. This is a physically credible thick-walled tower interior with warm-gray ashlar masonry, a narrow leaded daylight slit on one side and one modest bronze wall candle, dark sober oak handrails.
Show ONE clear onward route: a broad STRAIGHT RECTANGULAR FLIGHT OF STONE STAIRS occupying the RIGHT half and leading UP AND AWAY from the viewer toward a recessed pointed doorway near the upper CENTER RIGHT. Each tread is a rigid flat rectangular slab with identical riser heights and depths; both stair sides and the oak rail are straight in world space, perspective consistent. The first tread is completely visible above the lower landing at roughly x=59%-91%, y=87%; the flight rises toward a short level upper landing at roughly x=62%-81%, y=40%. Show thick load-bearing stone under the flight and upright stable wooden balusters. The upper pointed doorway, around x=58%-83%, y=18%-49%, opens into a short final exit recess illuminated by bright cool daylight; beyond the immediate threshold only a solid stone return wall and a narrow wash of sky light are visible. A final turn to the open-air lookout happens behind that opaque masonry, not as a warped visible bend. The upper recess and the straight flight form ONE selectable destination: the tower-top viewpoint. Both the stair silhouette and top doorway are legible, unobstructed and large enough for a click hotspot. Keep a clear foreground landing and a quiet solid left wall, avoid a maze.
No descending secondary route drawn in front, no separate side doors, no circular or spiral stair, no fan-shaped steps, floating steps, splayed handrail, impossible Escher geometry, wide open floor overlooking the hall, dungeon darkness, overgrown ruin or excessive cathedral tower scale. Refined believable stonework, brightening sky light as an invitation to emerge outdoors, no actual panoramic landscape visible yet.
